findings.breaking_input: A packed or adversarial `opencode export` JSON placed on the fake's stdout that makes `exportedSpend` recurse forever — e.g. deeply nested object `{"a":{"a":{"a":...}}}` thousands deep — or one with a huge number of sibling keys and values. The wrapper's `spawnSync` reads the export under maxBuffer 64 MiB, but `walk(j)` recurses with no depth limit and iterates every value with `Object.values(o)`, so a JSON constructed with 10^5 nested layers (few bytes each) or 10^6 keys in an object (within 64 MiB) drives unbounded recursion / billions of visited values; the wrapper blocks (synchronous) until the stack overflows or the event loop starves — never reaching the cap check or `COST-UNREADABLE`.
findings.why: `exportedSpend`'s `walk` visits every node (`for (const v of Object.values(o)) walk(v)`) with no depth cap or visited-set guard, and it runs in `charge()` synchronously inside the main event loop (`spawnSync` + `walk`) before the next event is read. A hostile/large export therefore stalls or crashes the wrapper, so the run is neither terminated at the cap nor reported COST-UNREADABLE — it can run past the cap forever or die with a stack overflow, defeating REQ-11 (a foreign-harness run cannot spend past its cap) exactly where subagent spend is the newly-added charge path.
findings.fix: Impose a depth bound (e.g. reject >64 levels) and a node budget (e.g. 50k) in `exportedSpend`, counting visited nodes incrementally and throwing `COST-UNREADABLE` on exceeding it.
findings.twin_of: (bo) a spend cap that trusts every event
